title: Unable to completely disable the Windows key. (Keyboard Manager)

fix_assessment.rationale: The stated examples fall within documented OS-reserved/Game Bar limitations, and a software remap does not repair malfunctioning hardware or guarantee complete key suppression.

comment.body: The two examples here have documented exceptions: Win+L is reserved by Windows and cannot be remapped, and Win+G can still activate Xbox Game Bar despite reassignment. Keyboard Manager therefore cannot guarantee complete suppression of a malfunctioning physical Windows key. That needs device-level repair or a hardware-supported way to disable the key, rather than a PowerToys patch to intercept protected shortcuts. This does not establish that every other mapping is broken; any additional ordinary shortcut failure should be described separately.

evidence: The reporter describes a physically malfunctioning Windows key and expects a software remap to disable every Windows shortcut.
The two concrete examples are Win+L locking and Win+G opening Xbox Game Bar.
Official Keyboard Manager documentation explicitly excludes OS-reserved Win+L and notes Win+G may still open Game Bar even when reassigned.
judgment.rationale: A normal-desktop hook is not a hardware/firmware key-disconnect mechanism and cannot promise suppression of protected shortcuts. Explain those exact exceptions without claiming the supplied configuration is validated or every other shortcut failure has the same cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Clarify documented limits and handle the malfunctioning physical key at the device level rather than proposing a protected-shortcut bypass.
